findings.issue: CreateOrganisation() wipes the serialized copy of the organisation seeds (plainSeeds) but never the DeviceSeeds arrays that identity.Export() handed back: `var seeds = identity.Export();` leaves two 32-byte private seeds (Ed25519 signing, X25519 agreement) of the organisation root on the managed heap after the method returns. `using var identity` wipes the identity's own copy, not the exported one. This is the most valuable secret the tool ever holds, and it is the only Export() call site in the solution.
findings.fix: Wipe it in the same finally that clears plainSeeds: `try { plainSeeds = CanonicalJson.SerializeToUtf8Bytes(seeds); sealedSeeds = _db.Seal(plainSeeds); } finally { Array.Clear(plainSeeds); CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory(seeds.SigningSeed); CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory(seeds.AgreementSeed); }`.

findings.issue: The round-3 medium is fixed for the normal path (verified live: keys\ held admin.key alone), but both deletion paths swallow failure silently — AdminKeyFile.TryDeleteBackup and AdminAccountService.RemoveRetiredKeyFileBackup catch IOException/UnauthorizedAccessException and carry on. A backup held open for a moment (a scanner, a backup agent) therefore survives a recovery still carrying the retired password's wrap of the very same database key, and nobody is told. The whole security promise rests on a best-effort delete.
findings.fix: Make a surviving backup harmless instead of only trying to remove it: in Save(), when keepBackup is false and a backup exists, first overwrite it with the new bytes (File.WriteAllBytes(backup, bytes)) and only then attempt File.Delete. A backup that cannot be deleted then holds the current wrap set rather than the retired one.

findings.issue: The exit guard added this round covers only the footer «الخروج» button (confirmed live: the red «إغلاق الأداة قبل حفظ ورقة الاسترداد؟» dialog appeared and the tool stayed open). The Windows title-bar close button still goes straight to the WPF window and destroys the only copy of the organisation recovery code with no question asked — the same irreversible act the round-3 finding described ("and the title-bar close does the same").
findings.fix: Give IAdminWindow a guard seam, e.g. `void SetCloseGuard(Func<bool>? guard)`; WpfAdminWindow stores it and MainWindow's Closing handler sets e.Cancel and raises the same AdminConfirmDialog when the guard says the sheet is unsaved. A01 registers `() => SheetUnsaved` and clears it on dispose.

findings.issue: WriteServedLockOuts() writes one audit row per served lock-out and AdminKeyFile.LockOutsToReport is unbounded, so somebody who keeps triggering lock-outs at the machine queues an arbitrary number of identical «قُفل الدخول مؤقتًا» rows that all land at once when the real administrator next signs in — the one screen (A11) meant to make an attack visible is where the flood arrives.
findings.fix: Cap the counter where it is raised in RecordWrongPassword (`keyFile.LockOutsToReport = Math.Min(keyFile.LockOutsToReport + 1, 20);`) or write a single row carrying the number in details (`["lockouts"] = count`), which also keeps the log readable.

findings.issue: OnStartup calls AdminHostPaths.Configure(), ConfigureRemoteDebugging() and ConfigureLogging() before the AppDomain unhandled-exception handler that ConfigureLogging itself installs. A data folder that cannot be created therefore kills the tool with the raw English .NET crash dialog and a full stack trace — I reproduced it (System.IO.IOException at AdminHostPaths.ResolveLogFolder, AdminHostPaths.cs:121). That is technical error text in front of the person, contrary to item 15, and it is reachable outside --data-folder whenever C:\ProgramData\WakeelAdmin cannot be written to.
findings.fix: Wrap those three calls plus AdminHostPaths.CreatePaths() in a try/catch for IOException, UnauthorizedAccessException, ArgumentException and NotSupportedException; on failure show an Arabic MessageBox («تعذّر على الأداة تجهيز مكان بياناتها على هذا الحاسوب.») and call Shutdown(1) instead of letting the exception escape.

findings.issue: The «هذا الجزء غير متاح في هذه النسخة بعد.» explanation for the two switched-off controls reaches the person only through WTooltip's `.w-tooltip-wrap:hover` rule. A disabled button is not focusable, so `:focus-within` can never fire and a keyboard-only user meets two dead controls with no reachable reason (confirmed in the live DOM: the bubble is present with role="tooltip" but nothing associates it with the button).
findings.fix: Point the button at the bubble — give the bubble an id and add aria-describedby to the WButton — or render the sentence as a small visible note beside the disabled control instead of relying on hover.

SECURITY. Argon2id wraps through Wakeel.Crypto with a fresh salt for the recovery wrap; the database key is random and lives only inside the two wraps, so a password change re-wraps rather than re-keys and the printed sheet survives. Org Ed25519/X25519 seeds are sealed with the database key before the row is written and the serialized plaintext is cleared in a finally (the exported DeviceSeeds arrays are not — finding 1); the org root goes through DeviceCertificate.IssueOrgRoot and its signature is checked against the stored public key in a test. SignIn/Recover split CryptoException correctly (WrongPassword/Tampered cost an attempt, everything else says the data is unreadable). Lock-out: 5 attempts, 30 s doubling with a half-hour ceiling, counter in the key file so a restart cannot erase it, now audited. DPAPI is registered machine-scope and deliberately unused by admin-1. --data-folder relocates the whole layout including the engine profile; WEBVIEW2_ADDITIONAL_BROWSER_ARGUMENTS is cleared before a validated port may set it; the BUILTIN\Users grant stays off keys\. No forbidden vocabulary (servers, ports, internet, PostgreSQL, Argon2, error codes) anywhere in AdminAr.

EXTENSION POINTS. AddWakeelAdmin(paths)+AddAdminAccount() TryAdd throughout with the host's real IAdminWindow/IAdminPrintService/IAdminImagePixels registered first; AdminRoutes already names A04–A11 and A03 reads its two routes through ForTab() once in OnInitialized, so admin-3 only adds them to Built and the buttons come alive with no change to A03; AdminAr is split by area with ownership stated per file; AdminSchemaMigrator is the admin tool's own embedded set.
